question: What is the main job of a skilled birth attendant during a home delivery?

options.A: To transport the mother to a hospital for every contraction
options.B: To prescribe long-term contraception before labor starts
options.C: To perform emergency cesarean sections in the home
options.D: To monitor mother and baby and manage normal childbirth

explanation: You've got this! A skilled birth attendant is simply there to watch how labor progresses, support the mother, and safely handle a normal delivery while keeping an eye out for any trouble. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why is having a solid backup plan to a hospital so important for home birth programs?

options.A: Most women prefer to give birth in a hospital eventually
options.B: Emergency situations can develop unexpectedly during labor
options.C: Community health nurses are not allowed to deliver babies alone
options.D: Hospitals require proof of home birth for birth certificates

explanation: Childbirth can take sudden turns! That's why having a fast, reliable link to a hospital is a must-have safety net just in case complications pop up. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h1)

question: Which of these means a planned home birth is definitely NOT safe?

options.B: Strong personal desire for home birth
options.D: Spontaneous onset of labor at term

explanation: Spot on. A uterus with a scar from a past CS has a risk of tearing during labor, so a hospital setting is much safer. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h2)

question: A woman carrying twins at 38 weeks asks to have her babies at home. What should you tell her?

options.A: Suggest waiting until labor is well established before deciding
options.B: Explain that multiple pregnancies require hospital care due to higher risks
options.C: Encourage home birth because twins are common in the community
options.D: Agree to attend the home birth if contractions are mild and regular

explanation: Great clinical thinking! Twin pregnancies carry higher chances of tricky presentations or heavy bleeding, so they truly need the safety of a health facility. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h2)

question: What is a key part of preparing ahead of time for a home birth?

options.A: Educating the family on recognizing pregnancy danger signs
options.B: Booking a hospital bed just in case labor fails to start
options.C: Purchasing expensive medical monitors for the bedroom
options.D: Administering routine general anesthesia at 36 weeks

explanation: Knowledge is power! Teaching the family signs like heavy bleeding or severe headaches helps them call for help early if something goes wrong. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h3)

question: During a home visit at 34 weeks, you notice the home has no clean running water or good lighting. What is your best move?

options.A: Ignore the issue since delivery is still weeks ahead
options.B: Help the family plan how to store clean water and arrange good lighting for the birth
options.C: Advise the mother to move to a relative's house in another town
options.D: Cancel the home birth plan immediately without discussing alternatives

explanation: As a supportive nurse, you help problem-solve practical needs with the family ahead of time so they are fully ready for the big day. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h3)

question: What is the main goal of using a clean delivery kit during a home birth?

options.A: To speed up the progress of the first stage of labor
options.B: To replace the need for handwashing by the birth attendant
options.C: To prevent infection for both mother and newborn
options.D: To provide entertainment for the family during labor

explanation: Simple and crucial—the kit provides clean, germ-free items to stop harmful bacteria from causing infections during and after birth. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h4)

question: Why is an oxytocic medicine a must-have in your home delivery bag?

options.A: To actively manage the third stage of labor and prevent bleeding
options.B: To help dilate the cervix more quickly in early labor
options.C: To relieve severe labor pain during the second stage
options.D: To stimulate milk production before the baby is born

explanation: You got it! Oxytocin makes the uterus clamp down strongly after delivery, which is our absolute best defense against heavy postpartum bleeding. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h4)

question: How do you usually check the baby's heartbeat during a normal home birth?

options.A: Using continuous electronic fetal monitoring belts
options.B: Using a fetoscope or Doppler at regular intervals
options.C: Checking the mother's pulse rate every fifteen minutes
options.D: Asking the mother how many times the baby kicks per hour

explanation: Spot on! Listening in at regular intervals with a simple fetoscope or Doppler is the standard, reliable way to make sure baby is happy inside. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h5)

question: Why is it important to encourage a laboring mother to empty her bladder often?

options.A: Urine samples must be tested every hour during home births
options.B: It stops the uterus from contracting too strongly
options.C: It prevents the development of chronic urinary tract infections
options.D: A full bladder can obstruct fetal descent and slow down labor

explanation: Think of the bladder like a roadblock in the pelvis! Emptying it clears the way so the baby's head can move down smoothly. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h5)

question: What is a major perk of delaying cord clamping for a healthy newborn?

options.A: It increases iron stores and placental blood transfer
options.B: It makes cutting the umbilical cord much easier for the nurse
options.C: It prevents the baby from developing neonatal jaundice
options.D: It speeds up the expulsion of the placenta from the uterus

explanation: Waiting just a bit before clamping lets that extra, valuable blood flow right from the placenta into the baby, protecting them against early anemia. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h6)

question: A baby is born limp, pale, and quiet after a home delivery. What should you do right away?

options.A: Immediately give the baby back to the mother for skin-to-skin contact
options.B: Wait patiently for five minutes to see if the Apgar score improves
options.C: Call an ambulance without taking any action inside the home
options.D: Provide initial steps of warmth, clearing the airway, and stimulation

explanation: Act fast and stay calm! A baby who isn't breathing needs immediate help: dry them, keep them warm, clear the airway, and gently stimulate them. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h6)

question: What is the most important thing to check on a mother right after she delivers?

options.A: Visual acuity and hearing reflex responses
options.B: Uterine tone and amount of vaginal bleeding
options.C: Serum electrolyte levels and kidney function
options.D: Bowel motility and digestive enzyme output

explanation: Safety first! Checking that the uterus feels firm and watching the bleeding amount helps you catch heavy postpartum bleeding early. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h7)

question: Why do we encourage mothers to start breastfeeding right after birth?

options.A: It prevents the mother from experiencing postpartum depression
options.B: It ensures the baby sleeps through the entire first night
options.C: It eliminates the need for any future vitamin supplements
options.D: It stimulates uterine contractions and helps milk production

explanation: Nature is amazing! Nursing releases oxytocin, which naturally helps the uterus contract down to reduce bleeding while getting milk flowing for baby. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h7)

question: Which complication is a top cause of mothers dying during home deliveries?
explanation: Heavy bleeding after birth happens fast and can be very dangerous—it's the leading killer of mothers in home birth settings. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h8)

question: You are managing a home birth, and the placenta won't come out after 45 minutes even with active management, while bleeding increases. What should you do?

options.A: Encourage the mother to stand up and walk around the room
options.B: Attempt manual removal of the placenta immediately using bare hands
options.C: Wait another hour because retained placenta is completely harmless
options.D: Initiate emergency transfer to a hospital while monitoring bleeding and vital signs

explanation: You made the right call. A retained placenta with extra bleeding is an emergency that needs quick hospital transfer to keep the mother safe. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h8)
